title: CS1 labs and midterm used for early integrity review
summary: Students complete weekly take-home C++ labs and an in-person paper midterm. AI and other external tools are prohibited for lab programming; instructors compare lab and midterm coding performance to prioritize manual academic-integrity review.

sources.title: Midterm Exam Outliers Efficiently Highlight Potential Cheaters on Programming Assignments
sources.evidence_quote: all programming is conducted within the zyBooks platform, with no external tools allowed

assessment.summary: Complete auto-graded weekly C++ lab programs and write code during a proctored midterm exam.
student_actions: Develop and repeatedly submit C++ lab solutions.
Write code on paper in the midterm free-response section.

outputs.artifact: C++ lab submissions and paper exam responses

student_role.description: All lab programming had to occur in zyBooks with no external tools; the paper exam was proctored.

grading.method: Auto-grading with immediate feedback, partial credit, and resubmissions for labs; TAs graded exam code with an instructor rubric.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.

reported_results: Two course offerings totaling 177 students; the outlier approach flagged 23 students and averaged 83% precision after instructor review.

evidence_excerpts.quote: all programming is conducted within the zyBooks platform, with no external tools allowed
